annotation.material_differences: Response A includes a specific operational commitment to use an approved way to confirm who received the package, but it does not mention checking for neighbours/concierge/reception or delivery exceptions/reroutes. Response B adds those broader recipient checks and delivery exception details, which could change the scope of information gathered. Response C is more minimal and omits some of A/B’s concrete checks, especially any mention of authorised recipient confirmation or broader delivery-context inquiries.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: All three answers share the core idea of gathering order, address, timing, tracking, and proof-of-delivery information while distinguishing facts from assumptions and avoiding unnecessary collection. However, B explicitly expands the set of relevant questions to include alternative recipients and shipment anomalies, which is a meaningful change in the information-gathering scope under the criteria. C is narrower and does not preserve all of the same concrete evidence commitments, so the three are not fully equivalent at the criterion level.
